questions.question: What are the three broad groups into which seaweeds can be classified based on pigmentation?
questions.expected_answer: Brown (Phaeophyceae), red (Rhodophyceae) and green (Chlorophyceae).
questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction to commercial seaweeds
questions.evidence_quote: Seaweeds can be classified into three broad groups based on pigmentation: brown, red and green.

questions.question: Which country is the largest producer of edible seaweeds, and what is its harvest volume?
questions.expected_answer: China is the largest producer, harvesting about 5 million wet tonnes.
questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction to commercial seaweeds
questions.evidence_quote: China is the largest producer of edible seaweeds, harvesting about 5 million wet tonnes.

questions.question: According to Chapter 2, what are the two main genera of seaweeds from which most agar is extracted?
questions.expected_answer: Gelidium and Gracilaria.
questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Seaweeds used as a source of agar
questions.evidence_quote: Most agar is extracted from species of Gelidium (Figure 1) and Gracilaria (Figure 2).

filter.chapter: Chapter 2: Seaweeds used as a source of agar

questions.question: Which seaweed species is the main source of agar in India?
questions.expected_answer: Gelidiella acerosa.
questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Seaweeds used as a source of agar
questions.evidence_quote: Gelidiella acerosa is the main source of agar in India.

questions.question: Where has Gracilaria been grown in lagoons and ponds in recent years according to Chapter 2?
questions.expected_answer: In Viet Nam, grown in lagoons and ponds in both the north and south.
questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Seaweeds used as a source of agar
questions.evidence_quote: A more concerted effort appears to have been made in Viet Nam in recent years, with a variety of species being grown in lagoons and ponds in both the north and south.

questions.question: What are the two principal processes used to remove water from gel in agar production?
questions.expected_answer: The freeze-thaw process and squeezing it out using pressure.
questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Agar
questions.evidence_quote: Then the water is removed from the gel, either by a freeze-thaw process or by squeezing it out using pressure.

questions.question: Why is the freeze-thaw process relatively expensive in agar production?
questions.expected_answer: Because of high refrigeration and energy costs.
questions.chapter: Chapter 3: Agar
questions.evidence_quote: Because of the refrigeration costs, this freeze-thaw process is relatively expensive, compared to the alternative described next

questions.question: According to Chapter 4, which brown seaweed genus harvested for alginate grows on the Pacific coast of North America?
questions.expected_answer: Macrocystis.
questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Seaweeds used as a source of alginate
questions.evidence_quote: Brown seaweeds that fulfil the above criteria are species of Ascophyllum, Durvillaea, Ecklonia, Laminaria, Lessonia, Macrocystis and Sargassum, although the last, Sargassum, is only used when nothing else is available

filter.chapter: Chapter 4: Seaweeds used as a source of alginate

questions.question: Under what circumstances is Sargassum harvested for alginate extraction?
questions.expected_answer: Only when nothing else is available, because its alginate is usually of low viscosity and poor gel strength.
questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Seaweeds used as a source of alginate
questions.evidence_quote: although the last, Sargassum, is only used when nothing else is available

questions.question: What chemical substance is used in carrageenan extraction to increase gel strength?
questions.expected_answer: Alkali.
questions.chapter: Chapter 7: Carrageenan
questions.evidence_quote: Alkali is used because it causes a chemical change that leads to increased gel strength in the final product.

questions.question: What are the two major seaweed species cultivated as raw materials for carrageenan production?
questions.expected_answer: Kappaphycus alvarezii and Eucheuma denticulatum.
questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Seaweeds used as a source of carrageenan
questions.evidence_quote: Most carrageenan is extracted from Kappaphycus alvarezii and Eucheuma denticulatum.

questions.question: What is the characteristic feature of semi-refined carrageenan (SRC) processing method?
questions.expected_answer: The carrageenan is never actually extracted from the seaweed.
questions.chapter: Chapter 7: Carrageenan
questions.evidence_quote: This is the method in which the carrageenan is never actually extracted from the seaweed.

questions.question: What rank of production does nori have in Japan list of marine aquaculture products?
questions.expected_answer: Nori has the highest production among products from marine culture in Japan.
questions.chapter: Chapter 8: Seaweeds used as human food
questions.evidence_quote: In Japan’s list of products from marine culture, nori has the highest production, followed by oysters, yellowtails and wakame

questions.question: What is the nutritional value of Porphyra (nori) in terms of protein content?
questions.expected_answer: Porphyra has a high protein content of 30 to 50 percent, of which about 75 percent is digestible.
questions.chapter: Chapter 8: Seaweeds used as human food
questions.evidence_quote: It is among the most nutritious seaweeds, with a protein content of 30–50 percent, and about 75 percent of that is digestible.

questions.question: Which three hydrocolloids extracted from red and brown seaweeds are commercially important?
questions.expected_answer: Agar, alginate and carrageenan.
questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction to commercial seaweeds
questions.evidence_quote: Various red and brown seaweeds are used to produce three hydrocolloids: agar, alginate and carrageenan.

questions.question: What has caused a revival of interest in using seaweeds for agricultural fertilizers?
questions.expected_answer: The rising popularity of organic farming.
questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction to commercial seaweeds
questions.evidence_quote: Today, with the rising popularity of organic farming, there has been some revival of the industry

questions.question: According to Chapter 2, why are species of Pterocladia collected and where are they mainly harvested?
questions.expected_answer: They are closely related to Gelidium and collected as sources of agar, mainly in the Azores (Portugal) and New Zealand.
questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Seaweeds used as a source of agar
questions.evidence_quote: Closely related to Gelidium are species of Pterocladia, and small quantities of these are collected, mainly in the Azores (Portugal) and New Zealand.

questions.question: In what zone does the brown seaweed Laminaria saccharina typically grow?
questions.expected_answer: In the upper sublittoral zone.
questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Seaweeds used as a source of alginate
questions.evidence_quote: Laminaria saccharina also grows in the upper sublittoral

questions.question: Why can lambda carrageenans not be processed by methods relying on potassium gel formation?
questions.expected_answer: Lambda carrageenans do not form gels with potassium and would therefore dissolve and be lost during alkali treatment.
questions.chapter: Chapter 7: Carrageenan
questions.evidence_quote: Lambda carrageenans do not form gels with potassium and would therefore dissolve and be lost during the alkali treatment.

questions.question: Which countries have a multi-century tradition of using seaweeds as direct human food?
questions.expected_answer: China, Japan, and the Republic of Korea.
questions.chapter: Chapter 8: Seaweeds used as human food
questions.evidence_quote: For several centuries there has been a traditional use of seaweeds as food in China, Japan and the Republic of Korea.
